questions.q: Why does the real fix need two separate parts instead of one?
options: Stopping the recurrence (named selection + crawler fix) and repairing the already-wrong partitions are two different problems; fixing only one leaves the other unresolved
Only one part is actually necessary and the other is optional
The two parts must be done in the opposite order for any reason
There is only one part to this fix, matching Lesson 13 exactly
questions.explain: A fix that only stops future recurrence leaves already-wrong historical partitions in place; a backfill without the structural fix would recur on the next schema change.

questions.q: What does selecting columns by name instead of position actually change in the ETL job?
options: Each named column resolves against the real header in every file, so files with or without sales_channel inserted mid-row now produce identical output columns
It makes the job skip reading any file that has extra columns
It has no real effect on how the job processes rows
It requires every file to have exactly the same number of columns to run at all
questions.explain: select("order_id", "customer_id", ...) resolves names against headers regardless of column order, removing the dependency on position entirely.

questions.q: What crawler setting change prevents this exact failure mode from recurring on a future schema change?
options: Configuring the native CSV classifier with header-based ("Has headings") column recognition instead of purely positional inference
Switching the crawler to run every five minutes instead of on demand
Deleting the crawler entirely so it can never misread anything again
Disabling schema detection in the crawler altogether
questions.explain: Header-based recognition matches columns by name on each crawl, so a future added/reordered column is picked up correctly instead of misaligned.

questions.q: Why is aws glue reset-job-bookmark a required step before re-running the ETL job on the affected date range?
options: The job has bookmarking enabled, so without the reset it would treat those dates as already processed and skip them, leaving the deleted partitions empty
Resetting the bookmark deletes the job definition entirely
Job bookmarks only affect Redshift, not Glue, so this step is unrelated
The bookmark must be reset before every single run, even unaffected ones
questions.explain: Lesson 3's job has bookmarking enabled; resetting it for that range forces reprocessing instead of skipping dates it believes are already done.

questions.q: What does the final re-validation step compare, beyond just re-running the Finance report query?
options: One specific order_id from the corrected report against that same row sampled directly from after.csv in Lesson 14, confirming a genuine match to the raw file
Only that the query executes without throwing any error
The total row count of the entire fact_orders table against itself
A comparison against the Beginner capstone's data, which is unrelated
questions.explain: The spot-check ties the corrected output back to the actual raw file contents, not just confirming the pipeline ran without error.
